title: Sales Team Participation and One-to-One Video
article_body:
Ellie Abbott thought she was applying for a job at La-Z-Boy Southeast. She did not know that within months, strangers would be walking into the store asking specifically if Ellie was there. She had not met these people. But they knew her. They had watched her videos. And when they finally walked in, they were ready to buy.

That is what happens when a sales team participates in content creation and appears on camera as subject matter experts. The buyers experience them before the first conversation. By the time the handshake happens, trust is already built.

## Why Your Sales Team Belongs in Your Content Strategy

Your best content ideas are not sitting in your marketing department. They are in your sales team's heads. Salespeople know exactly what buyers ask before they are ready to purchase. They know which objections repeat across every deal, which comparisons prospects always bring up, and which explanations finally move someone from hesitation to commitment. That knowledge, translated into articles and videos, produces content that is more relevant, more credible, and more useful than anything a marketer could invent from a distance.

When the sales team actively participates in content creation, three things happen. The content becomes more closely tied to actual sales conversations. The sales team is more likely to use that content in Assignment Selling because they had a hand in making it. And buyers begin recognizing the faces on those videos, arriving at sales conversations with a sense of familiarity that no cold email or LinkedIn message can produce.

## One-to-One Video: The Sales Email Most Teams Are Not Sending

Most sales teams still communicate with prospects the same way they did in 1996: plain text emails. These emails take longer to write than video for any message of real substance, they are regularly skimmed or ignored, and they carry none of the warmth, tone, or personality that actually builds trust.

One-to-one video changes all of that. When a salesperson records a short, personal video for a specific prospect — introducing themselves before a call, following up after a meeting, or checking in on a proposal — the responses are almost universally the same: 'I was so impressed you sent me a video. No salesperson has ever done that.' 'I love how personal your process feels.' 'I felt like I already knew you before our first conversation.'

That reaction is not because video email is technically sophisticated. It is because it is rare. Most salespeople will not do it. That rarity is the competitive advantage. The salesperson who sends a 90-second personal video in an industry where everyone else sends a boilerplate text email is immediately more memorable, more human, and more trusted.

## Getting Your Team on Camera

Camera confidence does not come naturally to everyone, and that is fine. It is a skill that develops with practice. The SIMPLE On-Camera Performance Checklist offers a practical starting point: smile before the camera starts rolling; imagine you are talking to a specific real person; follow the No Stop Rule and push through rather than starting over; stand when possible to use your full range of expression; tell stories rather than reciting facts; and focus on connection rather than trying to sound impressive.

Leadership sets the tone for whether the team embraces video. If the leader never sends a video email, the team will not feel the pressure to do so either. When leaders go first — sending video updates, recording short team messages, appearing in content alongside their salespeople — the organization follows. Some of the most impactful transformations IMPACT has seen happened after a business owner decided to put themselves on camera and gave the team permission to do the same.

key_questions.question: How do we get our salespeople to start contributing to content?
key_questions.answer: Start with the simplest input: ask them to share the top questions buyers ask most often before the first appointment. Those questions become articles and videos. Then invite them to appear on camera for short segments answering those questions directly. The transition from contributor to on-camera subject matter expert happens naturally when they see how buyers respond.

key_questions.question: What is a one-to-one video email?
key_questions.answer: A one-to-one video is a short, personalized video recorded specifically for one recipient and embedded in an email. Instead of writing a paragraph of text to introduce yourself or follow up after a meeting, you record a 60 to 90 second video speaking directly to that person. It is faster to record than to write for longer messages, it is far more personal, and it consistently produces responses that no text email ever generates.

key_questions.question: What tools do salespeople use to send video emails?
key_questions.answer: Platforms like Vidyard, Loom, and BombBomb make it simple to record and send personalized video emails. Most integrate directly with email clients. A salesperson can record, review, and send a video email in under two minutes.

key_questions.question: What should salespeople say in a one-to-one video email?
key_questions.answer: The key is to be genuine and direct, not scripted. Introduce yourself with your face visible, reference something specific to the prospect's situation, explain what you are sharing or what the next step is, and close with a clear action. The point is connection, not production quality. A slightly imperfect video that feels personal will outperform a polished script every time.

key_questions.question: Does sales team participation in content slow down the sales team?
key_questions.answer: Done well, it saves time. Content that answers the questions buyers ask most often eliminates the need for salespeople to answer those questions manually in every call. When your team creates a video that addresses the three most common objections, every salesperson on the team benefits from that video indefinitely. The investment of one hour of a salesperson's time can save dozens of hours across the team.
